column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/pleme-stack.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS PINS. pleme-stack is the ULTIMATE single-file consumer shim: a repo
# adopting it gets seven jobs and never writes yaml again. Six of the seven are
# gated by ONE expression shape — `github.event_name == '<arm>'` — so the whole
# workflow is a three-way dispatch on the trigger, with a fourth job stacked
# behind an AND of two inputs:
#   pull_request  ->  pre-merge, security-pr, caixa-drift-check
#   push          ->  release, caixa-render  (+ container, conditionally)
#   schedule      ->  security-scheduled
# The three claims worth holding still:
#   1. PR-time is SIGNAL-ONLY. Nothing on the pull_request arm releases, opens a
#      meta-PR, or builds an image. caixa-drift-check passes open-pr:"false"
#      where its push-time twin caixa-render passes "true", and the two are
#      separate jobs precisely so the event decides which behaviour you get.
#      Row `pull-request-with-container-inputs` is the load-bearing one: it
#      hands the PR arm a fully-armed container config and asserts `container`
#      still does not select. A container build pushes an image; PR-time must
#      never be the do-it side of that.
#      MEASURED LIMIT on that row, so nobody over-reads it: deleting
#      `github.event_name == 'push'` from container's own `if:` produces ZERO
#      violations. `needs: release` already skips container on every non-push
#      arm, because release's condition is the same event test — the guard is
#      doubled, and no case can separate the two. This table therefore pins the
#      OUTCOME (no image build on a PR) and cannot pin WHICH guard delivers it.
#      That is not fixable by adding a row: a case where release selects on a
#      non-push event does not exist, by construction.
#   2. `container` needs BOTH inputs, not either. Its condition ANDs the toggle
#      with a non-empty image, so three rows exist where one would look like
#      enough: toggle-off-with-image, toggle-on-without-image, and both-set.
#      Without the first two, a condition degraded to a single term would still
#      go green.
#   3. THERE IS NO CATCH-ALL. Every job names its event explicitly, so a
#      consumer who adds a fourth trigger — workflow_dispatch, release,
#      issue_comment — gets a workflow where LITERALLY NOTHING RUNS and the run
#      is green. Rows `unrecognised-event` and `empty-event` are that state
#      written down: `empty-event` is separate on purpose, because "the trigger
#      resolved to nothing" is a distinct failure from "the trigger was some
#      other named event", and it is the one a caller's own broken expression
#      produces.
# WHY IT EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran the sibling
# cargo-auto-release, reported SUCCESS, bumped + tagged + pushed, and published
# nothing — its ship job was silently skipped by a condition that was entirely
# correct. A deliberate skip and a broken skip were the same green tick, because
# nobody had written down which jobs must run for a given input.
# `github.event.repository.private` IS DECLARED IN EVERY ROW THOUGH NO `if:`
# READS IT, for two reasons, and both matter to the next reader:
#   (a) pleme-stack reads it twice, in caixa-drift-check's and caixa-render's
#       `runs-on`, to pick a self-hosted label so a private consumer is not
#       billed for metered minutes. That is a RUNNER SELECTOR, never a
#       selection gate — the job runs either way, somewhere else.
#   (b) It IS a selection gate one level down, inside auto-release.yml's ship
#       job, which pleme-stack reaches via `release`. Row `push-private-repo`
#       pins that privacy changes nothing HERE, so nobody reads a green table as
#       evidence the private path publishes.
# LIMIT, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISREAD. Five of these seven jobs are
# `uses:`-calls into other reusable workflows (pre-merge-gate, security-gate,
# auto-release, container-stack). This oracle does not model reusable-workflow
# `with:` propagation, so a job SELECTING here says the call is reachable and
# dispatched — it says nothing about which jobs run inside the called workflow.
# auto-release.yml and container-stack.yml need their own tables; the ones that
# have them (auto-release.cases.tsv) are checked by the same selftest.
pull-request
pull-request-with-container-inputs
push-no-container
push-container
push-container-toggle-off
push-container-toggle-on-no-image
push-private-repo
schedule
unrecognised-event
empty-event
